start.text: A long way down, and then shingle under your feet. From the top the fog looked like a floor. From underneath it's a lid: grey, low, a man's height over the stones, and the air under it still and cold and smelling of weed.

Out from the middle of the beach a quay of dressed stone runs into the sea, too well built for anything Thornwold would have put here. The Keepers' boat-stage. Somebody is sitting on the very end of it, looking out.
Under the cliff a driftwood fire burns in a ring of stones, and two men stand either side of it, not looking at each other, the way men stand who've been arguing a week.
Overhead, high on the cliff, the Northing's lantern makes a gold place in the wool. From down here it's the only warm thing in the world.
On the stage's end a lantern hangs from an iron bracket, gold behind horn. The Ridge Light's. Ottie's standing under it.
By the fire, with a lantern of his own held out in front of him, Hob Marl is counting heads, and getting four, and starting again.
By the fire, with a lantern of his own held out in front of him, Hob Marl is counting heads, and getting three, and looking up at the Northing's light, and making it four.
